info.title: Upheap API
info.description: A todo list that ranks itself.

post.summary: Signs in with an email address or a username, and a password.
post.description:
Each account gets a few attempts per time window, counted together whether it's named by email address or by
username, and so does each address or username without an account. Past that, attempts fail with `429` until
the window ends, and a successful sign-in starts the count over.

200.description: Signed in; sets the session cookie

422.description: `field_empty` (`field` `login` or `password`); not counted as an attempt

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the account may try again

post.summary: Ends the current session. Succeeds when there is none.
post.description:
Only the session cookie is ended. A bearer token is left alone, and the answer is still `204`: a client signs out
with `POST /oauth/revoke`.

post.summary: Creates an account with a personal team and heap, and signs in.

201.description: Registered and signed in; sets the session cookie

422.description: Invalid email, name or password, or `invalid_handle` with a `hint`

get.summary: The rough due times to offer in a due picker, for today in the request's timezone.

parameters.name: Time-Zone
parameters.description: The device's IANA timezone, for example `Europe/Berlin`. Labels and dates use it. Defaults to UTC.

get.summary:
Opens an invite link: the team's name, the maker's name and whether the link works, ended or was revoked. Anyone
holding the token may, signed in or not; with a session cookie or bearer token the answer also says where the
caller stands in the team (`viewer`). An expired or unknown session cookie counts as signed out.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The invite link's secret: the last part of the link, `{origin}/invite/{token}`.

401.description: `unauthenticated`: the bearer token is invalid, expired or revoked

post.summary:
Joins the link's team as a member. Takes the session cookie only, never a bearer token: joining is the person's
decision in their browser, not something a client holding a token can do for itself. The link must be working at
this moment, and must not have been made before the caller was removed from the team. Answers `200` with the team
unchanged when the caller is already in it, as member or admin, whatever the link's state. The link keeps
working for others.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The invite link's secret: the last part of the link, `{origin}/invite/{token}`.

401.description: `unauthenticated`: no session cookie, or the request carried a bearer token

403.description: `removed_from_team`: removed from the team after the link was made

post.summary:
Creates an account through the link, and joins its team as a member in the same act: the account, its personal
team and heap, the membership and the session are all made, or none is. Works whether registration is open or
closed on the server. Takes the same body as `/auth/register` and checks it the same way, and answers `409`
`invite_link_ended` or `invite_link_revoked` when the link isn't working at this moment, even if the username is
also taken. Sets the session cookie, replacing any the caller had. The link keeps working for others.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The invite link's secret: the last part of the link, `{origin}/invite/{token}`.

201.description: Registered, joined and signed in; sets the session cookie

422.description: Invalid email, name or password, or `invalid_handle` with a `hint`

get.summary: The signed-in user with their teams and heaps.

patch.summary: Changes the signed-in user's display name. Send the user's `version` in `If-Match`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The `version` of what is being edited, for example `"3"`.

get.summary:
The caller's live sign-ins by clients such as the CLI, the most recently used first. A sign-in is live while its
refresh token can still be used; ended and expired ones aren't listed.

parameters.name: Time-Zone
parameters.description: The device's IANA timezone, for example `Europe/Berlin`. Labels and dates use it. Defaults to UTC.

delete.summary:
Ends one of the caller's sign-ins: its access and refresh tokens stop working at once. Succeeds when it ended
within the last day; one that ended earlier is gone and answers 404. A bearer token may end its own sign-in; its next request is then refused as signed out.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The sign-in's `id`, from the list.

204.description: Ended, or ended within the last day

404.description: No such sign-in, or it isn't the caller's

get.summary: Checks an authorization request without approving it.
get.description:
The consent page calls this before it shows anything, so it never asks about, or sends the browser to, a request
the server would refuse. Once this succeeds, the client and the redirect URI are good, so a user who declines is
sent to the redirect URI with `error=access_denied` and the `state`, which the page adds itself.

parameters.name: response_type
parameters.description: Must be `code`.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: A registered client: `upheap-cli`.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: `http://127.0.0.1:<port><path>` or `http://[::1]:<port><path>`, with no query or fragment.

parameters.name: code_challenge
parameters.description: The S256 challenge of the client's PKCE code verifier.

parameters.name: code_challenge_method
parameters.description: Must be `S256`.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The client's value, sent back to the redirect URI with the code.

post.summary: Approves an authorization request for the signed-in user, from the consent page.
post.description:
Takes the session cookie only, never a bearer token: approving is the user's decision in their browser, not
something a client holding a token can do for itself. The code in `redirect_to` is good once, for ten minutes.

401.description: `unauthenticated`: no session cookie, or the request carried a bearer token

post.summary: Revokes a token, and with it every token of the sign-in it came from.
post.description:
Answers `200` for a token the server doesn't know too, as RFC 7009 asks, so the answer says nothing about which
tokens exist and revoking twice is fine.

post.summary: Exchanges an authorization code, or a refresh token, for an access token and a new refresh token.
post.description:
A refresh token is good once. Presenting one that was used already revokes every token of the sign-in it came
from, as someone else must hold a copy; so does presenting a code a second time within its ten minutes.

post.summary: Creates a team with the caller as its admin. The team starts without heaps.

409.description: `handle_taken` (`field` `slug`), by a team or a username

parameters.name: team

get.summary:
What happened to a team, newest first, as far as the caller may see: its name, members and display names, and
its heaps being created, renamed and archived. Membership and heap changes are shown to admins only.

parameters.name: team
parameters.description: The team's slug.

parameters.name: entity_id
parameters.description:
Only the history of this entity: an item, tag, saved view or parameter of the heap, or the heap itself; for
a team, the team, one of its heaps, or a member.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `next_cursor` from the previous page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1 to 200. Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: Time-Zone
parameters.description: The device's IANA timezone, for example `Europe/Berlin`. Labels and dates use it. Defaults to UTC.

post.summary: Adds a heap to the team. Admins only.

parameters.name: team
parameters.description: The team's slug.

parameters.name: team
parameters.description: The team's slug.

parameters.name: heap
parameters.description: The heap's slug, unique within the team.

patch.summary:
Renames the heap, changes its slug or writes its context; send the heap's `version` in `If-Match`. The name and
slug need an admin, the context any member. A body that sets a field the caller may not change is refused whole
with 403, and saves nothing. A save that changes nothing succeeds and keeps the version.

parameters.name: team
parameters.description: The team's slug.

parameters.name: heap
parameters.description: The heap's slug, unique within the team.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The `version` of what is being edited, for example `"3"`.

parameters.name: team
parameters.description: The team's slug.

parameters.name: heap
parameters.description: The heap's slug, unique within the team.

parameters.name: team

parameters.name: heap

parameters.name: entity_id
parameters.description:
Only the history of this entity: an item, tag, saved view or parameter of the heap, or the heap itself; for

get.summary:
The heap's non-closed items, ranked, with the reasons for each position. Ranking runs over every non-closed
item; the view then picks, groups and sorts what is returned, so filtered items keep their relative order.

parameters.name: team
parameters.description: The team's slug.

parameters.name: heap
parameters.description: The heap's slug, unique within the team.

parameters.name: as_of
parameters.description: The `as_of` from an earlier response, to keep the order stable. Omit to rank at the current time.

parameters.name: open
parameters.description: Where open items go. Defaults to `shown`.

parameters.name: in_progress
parameters.description: Where in-progress items go. Defaults to `pinned`.

parameters.name: blocked
parameters.description: Where blocked items go. Defaults to `hidden`.

parameters.name: blocked_layout
parameters.description: Whether shown blocked items get their own group or are mixed in with the open items. Defaults to `grouped`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: What each group is sorted by. Ties keep priority order. Defaults to `priority`.

parameters.name: sort_parameter
parameters.description: The parameter to sort by, a parameter of the same heap. Send it exactly when `sort` is `parameter`.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Keep items with any of these tags, comma-separated. Tags of the same heap.

parameters.name: effort
parameters.description: Keep items with any of these efforts, comma-separated.

parameters.name: impact
parameters.description: Keep items with any of these impacts, comma-separated.

parameters.name: need
parameters.description: Keep items with any of these needs, comma-separated.

parameters.name: param
parameters.description:
Options of the same heap's parameters, comma-separated. For each parameter they belong to, keep items with
any of its options listed. An archived option keeps the items that switched to its replacement.

parameters.name: Time-Zone
parameters.description: The device's IANA timezone, for example `Europe/Berlin`. Labels and dates use it. Defaults to UTC.

post.summary:
Adds a step to a task, at the end or right after the step numbered `after`, and answers with the whole item. The
new step is the one with the highest `number`. A task has at most 100 steps, dropped ones included. Adding needs
no `If-Match`; a step has its own version, and the item's `version` doesn't change.

parameters.name: team
parameters.description: The team's slug.

parameters.name: heap
parameters.description: The heap's slug, unique within the team.

parameters.name: item
parameters.description: The item's key, unique within the heap.

parameters.name: Time-Zone
parameters.description: The device's IANA timezone, for example `Europe/Berlin`. Labels and dates use it. Defaults to UTC.

patch.summary:
Edits a step of a task and answers with the whole item. `{step}` is the step's number. Send the step's `version`
in `If-Match`; the item's `version` doesn't change. A step can move from any state to any other.

parameters.name: team
parameters.description: The team's slug.

parameters.name: heap
parameters.description: The heap's slug, unique within the team.

parameters.name: item
parameters.description: The item's key, unique within the heap.

parameters.name: step
parameters.description: The step's number within its item: a positive integer, given when the step was added.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The `version` of what is being edited, for example `"3"`.

parameters.name: Time-Zone
parameters.description: The device's IANA timezone, for example `Europe/Berlin`. Labels and dates use it. Defaults to UTC.

404.description: No such item, or no step with that number

422.description: Invalid fields or `value_unknown` (a `state` the server doesn't know)

patch.summary:
Sets the heap's weights and its parameters' weights in one transaction. Admins only; send the heap's `version` in
`If-Match`. The heap's version orders saves through here, even those that change only parameter weights, and
each listed parameter's `version` is checked too. A parameter's own edits are guarded by its version alone. Weights equal to the stored ones are skipped, and a request that changes
nothing succeeds. Any error saves nothing.

parameters.name: team
parameters.description: The team's slug.

parameters.name: heap
parameters.description: The heap's slug, unique within the team.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The `version` of what is being edited, for example `"3"`.

get.summary:
The user whose username is `query`, users with a word of their display name starting with `query`, or, when `query` is the start of an email address
with at least its local part, `@` and one character of the domain, users whose email starts with it. Only for
admins of some team, to add members.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description:
A username, the start of a word of the display name, or the start of an email address up to at least `@` and one more
character. Ignores case. At least 3 characters.

403.description: The caller is no team's admin

label.description:
1 to 50 characters, unique among the parameter's options in use ignoring case. The new option comes last,
as the lowest priority.

AddStepRequest.description: A step to add to a task.

after.description: The number of the step the new one goes right after. Left out, the step goes at the end.

context.description: Plain text, at most 20,000 characters; blank means none.

replacement_option_id.description: Another option of the same parameter, in use. Open items with the archived option switch to it.

replaced_by_option_id.description: The option open items switched to. It may be archived too, with a replacement of its own.

options.description: Every option in use, exactly once, in the new order (highest priority first) and with its label.

AuditAction.description:
What was done. Each action is shown to those who may take it: members see item, tag and saved view changes,
admins see everything.

AuditChange.description: One changed field, ready to show.

before.description: `null` when it had no value, and for values with no short form, such as what a saved view shows.

field.description: The field as the diff names it: `title`, `tags`, or `parameters.<id>` for one parameter's value.

label.description: What it is called now: an item's title, a tag's name, a member's display name.

AuditEntityType.description: The kind of thing an entry is about. Members are `user`.

changes.description: The changed fields, in the order the entity's form shows them. Names are the current ones.

created_label.description: `created_at` in the request's timezone, such as "12 Mar 2027, 14:05".

diff.description:
The change as recorded, with IDs rather than names: `{"field": {"before": …, "after": …}}` for edits, the
values set for creations.

names_entity.description: Whether the entity's label goes after `phrase`. `false` when the entry is about the actor themselves.

phrase.description: What was done, to show after the actor's name: "edited item", "joined the team".

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last page.

ClientSignIn.description: One live sign-in of a client such as the CLI: the tokens it holds can still be used.

client_name.description: What to call the client, such as "Upheap CLI".

device_name.description:
What the client called the machine, such as its hostname. The client's claim and only a label. `null` for a
sign-in that sent none.

label.description: What to call this sign-in: the device name, else the client's `client_name`.

last_used_at.description: UTC milliseconds: when the sign-in last got new tokens.

last_used_label.description: How long ago it last got new tokens, in calendar days in the request's timezone: "today", "2 days ago".

signed_in_label.description: The day it was signed in, in the request's timezone: "today", "yesterday", "3 Nov", or "3 Nov 2025".

ClientSignInList.description: The caller's live sign-ins, the most recently used first.

ClosedGroup.description:
Which part of the closed list a closed item belongs in, in the request's timezone: `today` for the same calendar
day, `this_week` for 1 to 6 days before, and `earlier` for anything older.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last page.

Contributor.description: One labelled reason for an item's position.

share_percent.description: Share of the item's priority, 1 to 100.

need.description: Required: every item says how much it's needed.

parameter_values.description: An option for each parameter to set, by parameter ID: options in use of the same heap's parameters in use.

tag_ids.description: Tags of the same heap, at most 50.

slug.description:
Lowercase letters, digits and single dashes, starting with a letter, 2 to 39 characters. Leave it out to have
one made from the name: "My Team" gets `my-team`, or `my-team-2` if that is taken.

name.description: 1 to 50 characters, unique among the heap's parameters in use ignoring case.

options.description: Option labels, highest priority first: at most 50, unique ignoring case.

tag_ids.description: Tags of the same heap to suggest the parameter for.

weight.description: 0 to 100. Defaults to 10, the same as the heap's own weights.

name.description: 1 to 100 characters. Need not be unique.
1 to 50 characters, unique in the heap ignoring case.

Due.description: A due time, ready to show.

date.description: The calendar date in the request's timezone, `YYYY-MM-DD`, for date inputs.

firm.description: Exact deadline (`true`) or loose due time (`false`).

label.description: "in a few weeks" for loose due times; "tomorrow" or "12 Mar" for deadlines, in the request's timezone.

DueChoice.description:
A rough due time. Send its `date` as a loose due time (`firm: false`), and the item's due label comes back as this
`label`.

choices.description: Nearest first. The dates move with the day, so ask again on another day.

DueInput.description: A due time as entered: a calendar date, stored as the end of that day in the request's timezone.

archived_at.description: When it was archived, in UTC milliseconds; `null` while it is active. An archived heap is read-only.

context.description:
What the project is, where its knowledge lives, where work is reviewed and what finishing a piece means, as
written: plain text for now, Markdown later. `null` when nobody has written one.

open_count.description:
Items the heap's list shows by default, before filters: open and in progress ones, as the list's
`unfiltered_count` with the default view.

slug.description: Unique within the team; the heap's path is `/teams/{team}/heaps/{slug}`.

version.description: Send back in `If-Match` when renaming or changing the context or weights.

weights.description: The heap's ranking weights. Read-only here; admins set them with `PATCH …/weights`.

HeapAction.description: An action the caller can take on a heap.

open_count.description:
Items the heap's list shows by default, before filters: open and in progress ones, as the list's
`unfiltered_count` with the default view.

HeapOverview.description: A heap of one of the caller's teams, with how many items it has open.

HeapPatchRequest.description: A change to a heap. Leave a field out to keep it.

context.description:
At most 20,000 characters, trimmed; blank or `null` clears it. Any member may change it; the name and slug
need an admin.

slug.description:
Lowercase letters, digits and single dashes, starting with a letter, 2 to 39 characters. Links with the old
slug stop working.
Unique within the team; the heap's path is `/teams/{team}/heaps/{slug}`.

HeapWeights.description:
How much each of the heap's own ranking factors counts. A factor's share is its weight out of the total of all
weights, parameters' included; `0` turns the factor off.

age.description: 0 to 100. The weight of how long an item has waited.

deadline.description: 0 to 100. The weight of the due date.

value.description: 0 to 100. The weight of value per effort: effort and impact count together as one factor.

HeapWeightsPatchRequest.description: New weights for the heap and its parameters, saved together. Leave a weight out to keep it.

parameters.description: Parameters of the heap in use whose weight changes, each listed once.

HeapWeightsResult.description: The heap and its parameters in use after a weights save.

parameters.description:
The heap's parameters in use, by name, with their new versions: what `GET …/parameters` lists as
`parameters`.

HeldBack.description: One thing keeping an item from ranking higher, which the person could change.

label.description: Ready to show, for example "No due date".

Invitation.description:
What someone holding an invite link sees of it. Nothing else of the team or the maker is given: no IDs, no
members, no maker username or email.

created_by_name.description: The display name of whoever made the link, now, even if they have left the team.

state.description: Where the link is in its life. `ended` and `revoked` are shown too, so the page can say which.

oneOf.description: The caller's standing in the team; `null` when the request has no signed-in user.

InvitationAction.description:
An action the holder of an invite link can take. Empty unless the link works and admits the viewer: `join` for a
signed-in outsider, `create_account` for someone signed out.

InviteLink.description: An invite link: whoever holds its token can join the team until it ends or is revoked.

created_by.description: Who made it, by their display name now, even if they have left the team.

ends_label.description: `ends_at` as a date in the request's timezone: "today", "tomorrow" or "16 Nov".

token.description:
The secret, only while the link is `working`; `null` once it has ended or been revoked. A client builds the
link to share from it: `{origin}/invite/{token}`.

InviteLinkAction.description: An action the caller can take on an invite link.

InviteLinkList.description: A team's invite links, newest first.

InviteLinkState.description: Where an invite link is in its life. `ended` and `revoked` are final.

InviteRegistration.description:
What creating an account through an invite link answers: the new account, and the link's team as the new member
sees it, so a client can land them there without another call.

InviteViewer.description: A signed-in person's standing in the team a link is for.

team_slug.description: The team's slug, so the client can take a member to the team; `null` unless `status` is `member`.

InviteViewerStatus.description: Where a signed-in person stands in the team a link is for.

oneOf.description:
The item this one waits for. Set only on blocked items, and only when a blocker was picked. It can be
closed: finishing a blocker doesn't unblock what waits for it.

closed_at.description: UTC milliseconds; set exactly when the item is closed.

oneOf.description: Who closed it. `null` when the item is open, or was closed before who closed it was recorded.

Which part of the closed list it belongs in. `null` when the item is open. Clients group consecutive items
with the same group.

closed_label.description: When it was closed, ready to show ("yesterday", "3 Nov").

oneOf.description: Who added it. `null` only for an item added before creators were recorded, whose creation couldn't be traced.

created_label.description:
How long ago it was added, ready to show: "today", "yesterday", "4 days ago", "3 weeks ago", in the request's
timezone.

key.description: Five characters, unique within the heap and never changed; the item's path is `…/items/{key}`.

parameters.description:
A value, or `null`, for every parameter of the heap in use, and the item's values of archived parameters,
by parameter name.

oneOf.description:
How far the item has been prepared. `null` when the item is closed, and always in a build without the stage
(the static, single-user one).

stage_choices.description:
The stages the caller may set now, in table order: all three on an open task, the first two on an open note.
Empty when the item is closed, when the caller can't edit it, and in a build without the stage.

oneOf.description:
Ticked of open and ticked steps. `null` when the item has no open or ticked step. On every response,
lists included.

steps.description:
A task's steps in order, dropped ones included; empty for a note. `null` in the ranked list and the closed
list, which carry only `step_progress`: read the item for its steps.

ItemAction.description: An action the caller can take on an item. Clients show controls only for these.

ItemOption.description: The option an item has for a parameter.

archived.description: Closed items keep archived options; open items switch to the replacement.

ItemParameter.description: An item's value for one custom parameter.

oneOf.description: `null` when unset, which ranks as the parameter's lowest-priority option.

parameter_archived.description: Only closed items, and items reopened since, list archived parameters, and only when they have a value.

ItemPatchRequest.description: A partial edit. Leave a field out to keep it; send `null` to clear it.

blocked_by_item_id.description:
The item this one waits for: a non-closed item of the same heap. Only a blocked item can have one, so send
it with `"state": "blocked"` unless the item is blocked already. `null` clears it. Leaving the blocked state
clears it too.

kind.description: A note can become a task; `"note"` on a task is refused. Applied before `stage`. `null` is refused.

need.description: Need can be changed but not cleared; `null` is refused.

parameter_values.description:
Values to change, by parameter ID: an option in use to set, or `null` to clear. Parameters left out keep
their values.

stage.description: `"defined"` needs a task, or `kind` set to `"task"` in the same patch. `null` is refused.

tag_ids.description: Replaces the item's tags. Tags of the same heap, at most 50. Send `[]` to clear them; `null` is refused.

ItemRef.description: Another item, named where this one refers to it.

key.description: Unique within the heap; the item's path is `…/items/{key}`.

ItemTag.description: A tag on an item: enough to show it.

Kind.description: What an item is. A note becomes a task in place; a task never goes back to a note.

tag_ids.description: Tags of the same heap, at most 50. Replaces the parameter's tags; `[]` unlinks them all.

ListSort.description:
What the list is sorted by: `priority` (highest first), `due` (soonest first), `effort` (smallest first),
`impact` (largest first) or `parameter` (the custom parameter in `sort_parameter`, its first option first).
Items without the value come last.

ListView.description: A list view with every setting spelled out, as a saved view returns it.

effort.description: Keeps items with any of these efforts. Empty doesn't filter.

impact.description: Keeps items with any of these impacts. Empty doesn't filter.

need.description: Keeps items with any of these needs. Empty doesn't filter.

param.description:
Options of custom parameters. For each parameter they belong to, keeps items with any of its options listed.
Empty doesn't filter.

sort_parameter.description: The parameter the list is sorted by, when `sort` is `parameter`.

tag.description: Keeps items with any of these tags. Empty doesn't filter.

ListViewInput.description:
A list view to save. Leave a setting out for its default: in-progress items pinned, open items shown, blocked
items hidden and grouped, by priority, without filters. Send `sort_parameter` exactly when `sort` is `parameter`.

param.description: Options of the same heap's parameters.

sort_parameter.description: A parameter of the same heap, when `sort` is `parameter`.

tag.description: Tags of the same heap. Keeps items with any of them.

allowed_actions.description: Empty for the local build's one user, who can't sign out and has only the one team.

MeAction.description: An action the caller can take on their account.

MemberAction.description: An action the caller can take on one member.

Need.description:
How much an item is needed: what happens if it never gets done, from least to most.

- `idea`: kept so it isn't forgotten; nothing is lost if it never happens.
- `nice_to_have`: wanted, but nobody is waiting for it.
- `expected`: someone is counting on it; skipping it lets them down.
- `critical`: it has to happen; skipping it does real damage.

OAuthApproval.description: Where to send the browser now that the user allowed the request.

redirect_to.description: The request's redirect URI with `code` and `state` added.

OAuthAuthorizationRequest.description:
An authorization request, as the client put it in the consent page's address (RFC 6749 §4.1.1, RFC 7636 §4.3).
Every value is checked on the server; a missing one is refused with the problem for that value.

code_challenge.description: The S256 challenge of the client's PKCE code verifier.

redirect_uri.description: `http://127.0.0.1:<port><path>` or `http://[::1]:<port><path>`, with no query or fragment.

state.description: The client's value, sent back to the redirect URI with the code.

OAuthClient.description: The client an authorization request is from, once the request is known to be good.

display_name.description: What to call the client when asking the user, such as "Upheap CLI".

OAuthError.description: A refused token or revocation request (RFC 6749 §5.2). The token endpoints answer with this, not a `Problem`.

error_description.description: What was wrong, for people. May change; branch on `error`.

client_id.description: When given, a token of another client is left alone.

token.description: An access or refresh token. Either ends the client's sign-in.

token_type_hint.description: `access_token` or `refresh_token`. Accepted and not needed: the server finds the token either way.

client_id.description: A registered client: `upheap-cli`. Required with either grant, as the client is public.

code.description: With `authorization_code`: the code the redirect URI received.

code_verifier.description: With `authorization_code`: the PKCE code verifier the challenge was made from.

device_name.description:
With `authorization_code`: a name for the machine, shown in the user's list of sign-ins. Trimmed; at most 64
characters, no control characters. A client's claim, only a label. Ignored with `refresh_token`.

redirect_uri.description: With `authorization_code`: the redirect URI the code was issued for, exactly.

refresh_token.description: With `refresh_token`: the refresh token, which this request uses up.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the access token expires.

refresh_token.description: Good for one refresh, within 30 days.

OptionArrangement.description: One option of a new arrangement.

archived_at.description: UTC milliseconds; `null` while the parameter is in use.

archived_options.description: Archived options, in the order they were archived.

options.description: The options in use, highest priority first.

tag_ids.description: The tags whose items the parameter is suggested for.

weight.description: Influence on the ranking next to the heap's other weights, 0 to 100.

ParameterAction.description: An action the caller can take on a parameter.

archived.description: Archived parameters, by name. Closed items may still show their values.

parameters.description: The parameters in use, by name.

ParameterListAction.description: An action the caller can take on a heap's parameters.

ParameterPatchRequest.description: A partial edit. Leave a field out to keep it.

ParameterWeightChange.description: A new weight for one parameter, if it is still at `version`.

version.description: The parameter's `version` as the client last saw it.

ParameterWeightDraft.description: A draft weight for one parameter.

Problem.description: An error response body (RFC 9457 problem details).

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code, for example `version_conflict`.

field.description: The input field the error is about, when there is one.

hint.description:
A value of `field` that would be accepted, when the server can make one: the handle `invalid_handle` hints
at, such as `my-team` for `My-Team`.

request_id.description: Present on unexpected errors, so the operator can find the details in the log.

title.description: Short human-readable summary. May change; don't match on it.

contributors.description: The biggest reasons for the position, largest first.

held_back_by.description:
What keeps the item from ranking higher, in a fixed order: need, due date, sizes. Empty for the top item.
Only things a person could change, and only while the heap's weight for them is above 0.

as_of.description: The time the ranking used (UTC milliseconds). Send it back as `as_of` to keep the order stable.

blocked.description: Shown blocked items, when they're grouped. Empty by default, because blocked items are hidden.

hidden_count.description: How many items the filters keep but are left out because their state is hidden.

in_progress_count.description: How many of the heap's items are in progress, whatever the view and its filters leave out.

pinned.description: Items in pinned states (in progress by default), above the rest.

ranked.description: Items in shown states, including blocked items when they're mixed in.

unfiltered_count.description:
How many items the view would list without its filters (`tag`, `need`, `effort`, `impact`, `param`): the "14" in
"6 of 14". Hidden states still leave theirs out.

RankingPreview.description: The top of the list under draft weights. Nothing is saved.

as_of.description: The time both rankings used (UTC milliseconds).

items.description:
The first items of the ranked group (what `GET …/items` lists under `ranked` with the default view) under
the draft weights, in order.

RankingPreviewItem.description: An item near the top of the list under draft weights.

current_position.description: 1-based position of the same item in the same group under the stored weights.

RankingPreviewRequest.description: Weights to rank the heap with, without saving them. Leave a weight out to keep its stored value.

limit.description: How many items to list, 1 to 20. Defaults to 5.

parameters.description: Parameters of the heap in use to give another weight, each listed once.

username.description:
Lowercase letters, digits and single dashes, starting with a letter, 2 to 39 characters. Becomes the slug of
the personal team, and can't be changed later.

archived_at.description: When the view was archived (UTC milliseconds); `null` while it is in use.

view.description: What the view shows. The fields are the query parameters of `GET /teams/{team}/heaps/{heap}/items`.

SavedViewAction.description: An action the caller can take on a saved view.

views.description: The views in use, by name. Archived views are left out.

SavedViewListAction.description: An action the caller can take on a heap's saved views.

SavedViewPatchRequest.description:
A partial edit. Leave a field out to keep it; a `view` replaces the whole view, with defaults for what it leaves
out.

login.description: An email address, or a username. `email` is still accepted in its place.

Stage.description:
How far an item has been prepared, from least to most. Set by hand.

- `as_written`: just as it was put down.
- `with_context`: background has been added.
- `defined`: clear enough to start on. Only a task can be defined.

StateMode.description: Where items in one state go in the list.

context.description: Plain text; `null` when there is none.

number.description:
The step's number within its item, given when it was added and never changed or reused. The step is named
by its item's key and this number, as `k3x9a.3`, and its path is `…/items/{key}/steps/{number}`.

version.description:
Send back in `If-Match` when editing the step. A step has its own version; writing it never changes the
item's.

StepAction.description: An action the caller can take on a step. Clients show controls only for these.

StepPatch.description: A partial edit of a step. Leave a field out to keep it; send `null` to clear the context.

context.description: Plain text; `null` or blank clears it.

StepProgress.description: How far a task's steps have got.

total.description: Open and ticked steps. Dropped ones don't count.

StepState.description:
Where a step stands. A step can move from any state to any other.

- `open`: still to do.
- `ticked`: done.
- `dropped`: no longer wanted. The step stays, shown as dropped, and doesn't count in the item's progress.

TagAction.description: An action the caller can take on a tag.

TagListAction.description: An action the caller can take on a heap's tag list.

TagPatchRequest.description: A partial edit. Leave a field out to keep it; send `null` to clear the description.

Team.description: A team with its members and heaps, as the caller sees it.

personal.description: Whether this is the caller's personal team: theirs alone, with their username as its slug.

slug.description: Unique among teams and usernames; the team's path is `/teams/{slug}`.

TeamAction.description: An action the caller can take on a team.

TeamPatchRequest.description: A change to a team. Leave a field out to keep it.

slug.description:
Lowercase letters, digits and single dashes, starting with a letter, 2 to 39 characters. Refused with
`personal_team` on a personal team. Links with the old slug stop working.

member_count.description: Everyone in the team, the caller included.

personal.description: Whether this is the caller's personal team, which is theirs alone.

role.description: The caller's role in this team.

username.description: Also the slug of the user's personal team. Never changes.

version.description: Send back in `If-Match` when changing the display name.

UserMatch.description: Only what an admin needs to pick the right person.

email.description: Only when the query matched the start of the email, so a lookup by name never reveals addresses.

UserRef.description: A user, named where something refers to them: who made an audit entry, who added an item.

tags.description: A heap's custom parameters and their options
